name: Slovenia

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally
paths.note: Dividends bear a 25% final tax with a credit for foreign withholding (ZDoh-2 Art. 132). Gains bear 25%, 20% after 5 years, 15% after 10 years and 0% after 15 years of holding per lot; the tax file scores the long-held 0%. Children and spouse are exempt from inheritance tax (ZDDD Art. 9); there is no wealth tax.

paths.name: Family holding d.o.o.
paths.note: A Slovenian d.o.o. owned by the parents holds the portfolio. It pays 22% corporate income tax (2024-2028) on every realised gain (the 50% gains exemption needs an 8% stake and an employee) and about 1.1% on dividends (excluded from the base, with 5% added back). Payouts bear 25% again. The parents' estate holds the d.o.o. shares; children are exempt from inheritance tax. Rarely better than personal holding: gains inside the company are taxed at 22% where a long-held personal position pays 0%.

checks.working: Foreign dividends 20,000: 25% final tax (Art. 132 ZDoh-2; FURS guide of 4 Aug 2026, section 3.3) = 5,000. Foreign tax paid is deducted from the Slovenian tax in proportion, up to that tax (FURS guide, question 12): the 15% withholding of 3,000 is below 5,000, so the tax is 5,000 - 3,000 = 2,000. Gains 15,000 are taken from lots held over 15 years: not taxed ('po 15 letih imetnistva', FURS guide, list 'Oprostitev placila dobicka iz financnega kapitala'; 15 years since 1 Jan 2022, 20 before). Total 2,000. The EUR 1,000 allowance applies only to bank interest, not dividends.

Corporate income tax 22% for 2024-2028 (Art. 64 ZORZFS; FURS 'Davek od dohodkov pravnih oseb'). Dividends 20,000 are excluded from the base (Art. 24 ZDDPO-2) but 5% of the dividends received, 1,000, counts as a non-deductible expense (FURS guide 'Splosno o DDPO', section 5.1). The foreign withholding of 3,000 is booked as tax outside the profit and the exclusion is taken on the gross dividend (FURS 0920-13147/2022-3), so no credit is claimed. Gains 15,000 on listed minority holdings get no exemption (50% only for a stake of at least 8% held 6 months with an employee): fully taxable. Taxable profit 1,000 + 15,000 = 16,000 x 22% = 3,520. The company's own running costs are not in the tax file. Payout tax (25% on distributions) excluded.

The inheritance and gift tax (ZDDD) is charged on the recipient; children, adopted children and their descendants, the spouse and the partner of the deceased are in the first inheritance order and are exempt (Art. 9 ZDDD; FURS 'Dedoval sem'). Each child receives 3,333,333.33, tax 0. Inheritance is not a disposal for income tax, so no capital gains tax arises at death.

The d.o.o. shares (worth about 10,000,000) pass to the three children as first-order heirs, exempt from inheritance tax (Art. 9 ZDDD). Death is not a disposal for income tax, and the company's own tax position does not change. Tax 0.

assumptions: Checks use the top rates for a family with about EUR 600,000 of dividends a year: dividends at the flat 25% (no progressive scale applies to capital income), the company at the flat 22%.

Personal gains are taken from lots held over 15 years, as the tax file does. A rebalanced portfolio would realise part of its gains at 25%, 20% or 15%; the engine cannot vary the rate by holding period, so the projection scores the long-held 0%.
The holding period of positions bought before the move is assumed to run from their original purchase date (not from the date of arrival).
Small allowances are left out (EUR 1,000 on bank interest does not touch dividends). Foreign dividends carry 15% withholding, within the treaty rate.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: personal gains tax falls with holding period (25% to 5 years, 20% to 10, 15% to 15, 0% after 15 years, ZDoh-2 as in the FURS guide); the tax file holds one rate per asset class, so the 60-year projection cannot show a family that rebalances and pays 25% on part of its realised gains.

Private foundation and trust were considered and not added: a thesis abstract (University of Ljubljana, 2018) says Slovenian law allows private foundations only for public-benefit purposes; not checked against the statute.

ZDDPO-2 article numbers (24, 25) and the 5% add-back come from the FURS guides and PwC; the statute text at PisRS could not be read. Whether foreign withholding is creditable on an excluded dividend (Art. 75) is assumed not.
The 22% corporate rate is temporary (2024-2028; 19% after): the tax file uses 22% for all years of the projection.
